logline: A fictionalized Larry David navigates the absurd social minefields of Los Angeles life, turning minor etiquette violations into epic, escalating catastrophes.

renewal.note: The 12th and final season concluded on April 7, 2024. Larry David confirmed it as the series finale after 24 years on air.

bollymeter.basis: The debut season earned 89% on Rotten Tomatoes and established the improvisational cringe-comedy template that would define a genre. Larry David's singular social obliviousness landed as both specific and universally recognisable.

seasons.review_body: The first season of Curb Your Enthusiasm arrived in October 2000 as a loose, improvisational follow-up to Larry David's 1999 HBO special. The 89% Rotten Tomatoes score reflected broad approval for a show built entirely on improvisation and the gap between social expectation and human reality. The format - no script, just Larry David's comic sensibility and a cast calibrated to follow it - gave every scene an unpredictable texture. The Guardian later ranked the series 13th among the greatest television shows of the 21st century. The debut season was where that singular comic worldview found its structural home.

bollymeter.basis: A perfect 100% on Rotten Tomatoes. The improvised ensemble was fully locked in, with Larry David's social obliviousness escalating from quirky to cosmically inevitable.

seasons.review_body: Season 2 achieved a rare 100% on Rotten Tomatoes, cementing the series as something more than a Seinfeld postscript. The improvisational format had matured: David's supporting ensemble - Jeff Garlin, Cheryl Hines, Susie Essman - were now fully calibrated comedic foils rather than reactive props. The season's escalating social catastrophes felt less like sketches and more like an argument that polite society is a thin fiction. The perfect RT score was unambiguous endorsement.
seasons.season_over_season: A step up from Season 1's foundation - the ensemble chemistry is now fully established and the comic escalations hit with more precision.

bollymeter.basis: Season 7 earned 97% on Rotten Tomatoes and is the series' creative peak by any measure. The Seinfeld reunion concept gave the season a structural arc that transformed the show's usual episodic comedy into something closer to serialised farce.

seasons.review_body: Season 7 is the pinnacle of Curb Your Enthusiasm's 24-year run by critical measure: 97% on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic 81. The conceit - Larry David orchestrating a fictional Seinfeld reunion to win back his ex-wife Cheryl - allowed the series to operate on two satirical levels simultaneously: as a comedy about show-business nostalgia and as a dissection of male self-deception. The actual reunion sequences, featuring the original Seinfeld cast, were a TV event. The 97% Rotten Tomatoes score reflected near-unanimous enthusiasm across the press run.
seasons.season_over_season: The Seinfeld reunion arc elevates Season 7 from episodic comedy to the series' most ambitious structural experiment.

episode_reviews.title: Seinfeld
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The season finale delivers the long-promised Seinfeld reunion within the show's meta-fictional frame. Every comedic thread from the season pays off in the same room, and the episode functions both as fan service and as a sharp commentary on television nostalgia and the ego of creators.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The Seinfeld cast reconvenes on the set - a moment that collapsed two decades of pop-culture memory into one scene.

bollymeter.basis: Season 9 scored 74% on Rotten Tomatoes - the series' low mark - after a six-year hiatus. Some topical material landed sharply; other plots felt like the show reconnecting with itself rather than advancing.

seasons.review_body: Season 9 arrived after a six-year gap - the longest in the series' run - and the 74% Rotten Tomatoes score (Metacritic 74) reflected the unevenness of a show reconnecting with its own rhythms. The topical material felt grafted onto the show's usual social-cringe architecture rather than emerging from it organically. The core pleasures - David's confrontations with social norms, the precise comedic timing of the ensemble - remained intact, but the season as a whole felt like a reset rather than a statement. Still a net positive on the strength of individual scenes.
seasons.season_over_season: A step down from the heights of Seasons 7 and 8 - the six-year hiatus shows in uneven material, though David's core voice remains sharp.

bollymeter.basis: Season 11 scored 94% on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic 89 - the show's best since Season 3. The pandemic-era setting gave David's social-cringe engine fresh, specific material.

seasons.review_body: Season 11 represented a late-career creative surge: 94% on Rotten Tomatoes and Metacritic 89, the show's best since early peak seasons. The pandemic setting - Covid protocols, masked interactions, the policing of social space - turned out to be ideal territory for a show built on the argument that politeness is a contested fiction and David is uniquely committed to exposing it. Rolling Stone ranked the overall series 39th among the greatest television shows of all time in 2022. Season 11 was the episode run that earned that placing.
seasons.season_over_season: A sharp creative rebound from the mid-series dip - the pandemic setting gave David's social-cringe engine genuinely new material.

bollymeter.basis: The final season scored 94% on Rotten Tomatoes and Metacritic 82. The farewell landed as fitting and generous, with a finale that brought the series' 24-year run to a self-aware, characteristically unsentimental close.

seasons.review_body: The 12th and final season aired from February to April 2024, closing 24 years of Curb Your Enthusiasm with a 94% Rotten Tomatoes score and Metacritic 82. The conclusion resisted sentimentality while honoring the scale of what the show had achieved. The Writers Guild of America had ranked the series 30th among the 101 Best Written TV Series as early as 2013; the finale confirmed that legacy. David ended on his own terms and on creative high ground - a rarity for a comedy running past its 20th year.
seasons.season_over_season: A genuinely satisfying farewell - the final season finds Larry David at his most self-aware without sacrificing the confrontational comic edge that defines the series.
